Moving in San Diego

Where are you moving?

Moving a 1-bedroom apartment across San Diego costs $380–$960, with 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour, at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras. That is how much do movers cost in San Diego at the baseline. An elevator booking, a hunt for beach-area parking, a steep canyon driveway or a summer weekend can each add billed hours on top.

How much do movers cost in San Diego by the hour and by the day?

Moves within San Diego are billed by the hour for the crew and the truck. Each mover adds $50–$75 an hour, so a 2-mover crew for a 1-bedroom charges $100–$150 an hour, a 3-mover crew for a 2-bedroom $150–$225 an hour, and a 4-mover crew for a 3-bedroom $200–$300 an hour. Those rates come from the national rate table behind the calculator, not from San Diego quotes, and local price guides often publish higher hourly figures. Use them as the yardstick for how much do movers cost in San Diego when you read written estimates.

Some people think in days instead of hours. A crew booked for a full 8-hour day costs its hourly rate times eight, plus any base fee and travel time. Many local movers charge a base fee before the hourly billing starts, and a minimum of two hours or more is common, so a short job never costs only its hours. For a whole home, the total matters more than the rate: a 2-bedroom move at baseline costs $720–$1,800 and a 3-bedroom move $1,150–$2,850.

Condo towers, elevators and loading docks

Downtown, Little Italy, East Village and Bankers Hill are full of condo and apartment towers, and a tower move runs on the building's schedule. Most buildings ask you to book the freight elevator and the loading dock for a set window, and many ask the mover for a certificate of insurance before the crew can start. Some homeowners associations charge a move-in or move-out fee as well. Ask yours, because that fee sits outside how much do movers cost in San Diego on the mover's bill.

Every minute the crew waits for an elevator, walks a long corridor or rolls a dolly from the dock to the far end of a floor is billed. Book the first elevator slot of the day, send the certificate request to the mover a week ahead, and measure your largest furniture against the elevator door. A tower move that runs to schedule keeps how much do movers cost in San Diego close to the baseline for your home size.

Beach streets and canyon driveways

Near the coast, the problem is parking. In Pacific Beach, Mission Beach and Ocean Beach, many homes sit on narrow streets, courts and alleys, and curb space fills early on a summer weekend. When a full-size truck can't get close, the crew carries farther or shuttles loads in a smaller truck, and many estimates list a long-carry or shuttle charge on its own. Describe the street, the alley and the distance from the curb to your door when you ask for an estimate, so how much do movers cost in San Diego on paper matches the day.

Inland, San Diego's canyons and hills bring a different problem. Homes along the canyon rims, in parts of Mission Hills, Kensington and Clairemont, can have steep driveways, long stairs down to the front door, or no room for a truck to turn. The calculator asks about stairs and adds crew time for them. Answer it honestly, because stairs are where how much do movers cost in San Diego rises fastest for a house.

When San Diego movers are busiest

San Diego's weather is mild most of the year, as the weather panel below shows, so the season matters more for demand than for comfort. The calculator prices any date from May through September as peak season, and San Diego's summer adds its own rush: students moving to and from San Diego State and UC San Diego, and military families on orders around Naval Base San Diego, Marine Corps Air Station Miramar and Camp Pendleton. Month-end dates and weekends book first.

A weekday in the middle of the month, from October through April, is the easiest way to lower how much do movers cost in San Diego without changing the move itself. If you have to move in summer, book two or three weeks earlier than you would in winter, and take a morning start before the beach traffic builds.

A 2-bedroom move from Hillcrest to Chula Vista

Say you're moving a 2-bedroom apartment on the third floor of a Hillcrest building with an elevator to a two-story townhouse in Chula Vista, about 12 road miles south on Interstate 5 or Interstate 805. A typical local 2-bedroom move costs $720–$1,800 at the baseline, with a crew of 3 at $150–$225 an hour, off peak, with no stairs or extras. The real details then raise how much do movers cost in San Diego for this one:

  • the elevator has to be booked, and waiting for it is billed time;
  • the townhouse stairs add carrying time for every bedroom's furniture;
  • a Saturday in July puts the job in peak season, when crews book up first;
  • a packing service for 2 bedrooms adds $500–$1,200.

Pick a Wednesday in November, pack the boxes yourself and book the first elevator slot, and much of that falls away. Enter both ZIP codes, your floor, your stairs and your date in the calculator above to see how much do movers cost in San Diego for this move or your own. It's free and needs no email to see the price.

California rules for a San Diego move

The state's Bureau of Household Goods and Services (BHGS) licenses movers that carry household goods within, into or out of California. A mover handling a move into or out of the state must also be licensed by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). For a move within California, BHGS requires a visual inspection of your belongings for the estimate, and the moving agreement should show a Not to Exceed Price.

  • Moves out of state. For a move to Arizona, Nevada or anywhere else, you and the mover both sign the estimate. It should say whether it is binding, which guarantees the total unless you ask for more services, or non-binding, where the final cost follows the actual weight of the shipment.
  • Moves to Mexico. BHGS does not regulate international moves, so a move to Tijuana, Rosarito or elsewhere in Baja California falls outside its rules. Use a company that handles international shipments, and ask how it prices the customs paperwork.
  • Storage. BHGS does not regulate storage facilities either, so if your belongings wait in storage between homes, read that contract on its own.

Within the state, the 100-mile line applies too: a move to Los Angeles, about 120 road miles north, is charged by weight and mileage, not by the hour. Check a mover's license with BHGS before you pay a deposit, since unlicensed movers are among its most common complaints. A quote from an unlicensed company for how much do movers cost in San Diego carries none of these protections.

Leaving San Diego: weight and miles

The migration panel below shows where households leaving San Diego County go, and a long move to any of them is priced by the weight of the shipment and the miles. A 2-bedroom home moved 1,000 road miles, roughly the drive to Denver, costs $2,600–$5,700, off peak, with no stairs or extras. Spread over the distance, that is about $2.60–$5.70 per mile, a figure for comparing quotes rather than a rate movers bill by. On a move out of state, how much do movers cost in San Diego depends far more on what you own than on the hours.

Bringing how much do movers cost in San Diego down

  • Pick a quiet date. A mid-month weekday from October through April avoids peak-season pricing and the summer rush.
  • Book the elevator and the curb first. A confirmed elevator slot and a clear spot for the truck save more crew time than anything else on moving day.
  • Pack it yourself. A medium box costs $1.82–$2.69 each and a 10 lb pack of packing paper $19.99–$40.00, by typical published prices.
  • Use a container if you have a driveway. Each container trip costs $74.99–$150.00 by typical published figures, though most condo towers have nowhere to put one.
  • Compare written estimates. The moving companies panel below shows how many companies work in San Diego County, so there is room to shop around.

Take the calculator's range, two or three written estimates made after a visual inspection, and a booked elevator slot or curb space. Together they turn a general figure into a firm answer to how much do movers cost in San Diego for your own move.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • In San Diego, May, June, July, August, September and October are the mildest, driest months to move, by NOAA's 30-year averages.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • In San Diego, 1 in 7 people moved in the last year, against 1 in 8 across the US.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • Most hand laborers and material movers in the San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad, CA metro area earned $18 to $23 an hour in May 2025, against $17 to $23 across the US.
  • More households moved to San Diego County from Los Angeles County, CA than from any other county in 2022-2023: 6,449.
  • San Diego County had 150 moving companies with paid employees in 2023: 4.6 per 100,000 residents, against 2.8 across the US.
  • San Diego movers bill local moves by the hour, so elevator waits, long carries and steep driveways all show up on the bill.
  • Within California, a move of more than 100 miles, such as San Diego to Los Angeles, is charged by weight and mileage.
  • California's household mover rules don't cover international moves, so a move to Mexico needs its own checks.

Tipping a crew after a San Diego tower move

A tip isn't part of how much do movers cost in San Diego on the bill. Work out what tipping guides suggest per mover and for the whole crew, by the hours on site.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Questions

How much do movers cost in San Diego, from beach rentals to canyon homes? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

What items won't San Diego movers take on the truck?

Movers generally refuse hazardous materials such as gasoline, propane tanks, paint, aerosols and cleaning chemicals, along with perishable food, plants and pets. Most also ask you to carry cash, jewelry and important papers yourself. Ask each company for its list before you pack, so nothing left behind on moving day adds a second trip to how much do movers cost in San Diego.

How much should you tip on a San Diego move of a few hundred dollars?

Tipping is up to you. Many guides suggest 10% to 20% of the bill, shared among the crew, or $10.00–$20.00 per mover for a job of up to 4 hours. The tip calculator on this page works out both, and the tip comes on top of how much do movers cost in San Diego on the bill.

Why do San Diego moving quotes differ so much for the same home?

Each company sets its own hourly rate, minimum hours, base fee and travel charges, and some estimate the hours more honestly than others. A busy market like San Diego's widens the gaps between companies. Compare totals made after a visual inspection, not hourly rates alone, and hold them against the calculator's range for how much do movers cost in San Diego.

How much do movers cost in San Diego for a move to Los Angeles?

Los Angeles is about 120 road miles from San Diego, past California's 100-mile line, so the move is charged by weight and mileage rather than by the hour. It costs more than a move across town but well below a 1,000-mile move, which runs $2,600–$5,700 for a 2-bedroom home off peak. Enter both ZIP codes in the calculator to see how much do movers cost in San Diego for that route.

What extra charges show up on San Diego moving bills?

The common ones are a base fee before the hourly billing starts, a minimum number of hours, stairs, a long carry or a shuttle truck where the big truck can't park, and packing materials. A building's move-in fee is separate again. Ask for every charge in writing before moving day.
